subject: Regional comp surface adjustment — proposal for remote hires
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional comp surface adjustment — proposal for remote hires

Hi Karthik and Monica,

As we scale hiring for the next two quarters I want to formalize a lightweight approach to location-based adjustments for remote offers. Hiring teams are asking for guidance when candidates are US-remote in low-cost metros (e.g., Columbus OH) vs high-cost metros (e.g., SF) and when candidates are in EU/APAC jurisdictions.

Goal: produce a short, predictable set of levers hiring managers can apply so offers are consistent and defensible. Draft spreadsheet attached (2027_regional_adjustment_draft.xlsx) with a proposed:
- US: 3-band modifier (low / market / high) tied to our US paybands
- EU: country multipliers on top of base band (note social tax differences)
- APAC: a hybrid approach (multiplier + small location stipend)

Specific asks:
1) Karthik — can you review the proposed band multipliers and call out any sizing issues, particularly for engineering IC levels?
2) Monica — from an HR ops perspective, what operational hurdles do we face (offer letters, local statutory benefits, payroll)? Any budget guardrails we should add?
3) If this looks sensible, I'd like to pilot on the current hiring queue (3 software ICs, 1 product) next month.

Thanks — attaching the draft and a short example offer calculation for an L4 SWE.

—
Lauren Bishop
VP, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional comp surface adjustment — proposal for remote hires

Lauren — thanks for putting this together. Quick notes inline and a couple of recommended changes: 

- US bands: the 3-band approach makes sense. Suggest we tighten the upper band for L5+ eng ICs to avoid over-allocating against comp commits (i.e., band_high = band_med * 1.12 instead of 1.2).
- EU multipliers: rather than country-by-country to start, propose tiers (Nordics / Western EU / Eastern EU) — easier to maintain and avoids pushback.
- APAC: Singapore & Sydney should be treated like high-cost metros; others follow a regional multiplier with a small locality stipend to account for benefits variance.

Operational ask: we should add a "cap delta" field in the spreadsheet so hiring managers can't exceed the published band without a formal exception. Otherwise offers will drift.

Quick FYI: I've added a column for total on-target comp in the draft; see tab "summary".

-On Karthik
Engineering Comp Lead

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional comp surface adjustment — proposal for remote hires

Appreciate the clear asks. Operational considerations: 

- Offer letters: our current offer template supports an "additional stipend" line, but local statutory language varies — we'll need localized appendix language for certain EU countries (FR, DE).
- Payroll: for contractor vs employee classification in APAC we need to confirm legal for each market; that will influence total employer cost significantly.
- Budget guardrails: recommend a 7% program-level buffer for the pilot (to cover accepted offers that end up at the top of the band). Also recommend approvals for band exceptions routed to People Ops + Finance for anything > band_mid + 10%.

I can work with Legal to draft the localized appendices once we finalize multipliers. Happy to run the pilot administration (offer emission + acceptance reporting).

-Monica
Sr. Manager, People Ops

From: Ben Turner <ben@globalcomp.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional comp surface adjustment — proposal for remote hires

Hi Lauren — appreciate the context and the draft. Attached is a short benchmark (GlobalComp_benchmarks_Jun2027.pdf). High-level takeaways: 

- US: your 3-band approach aligns with market practice. For L4-L6 eng ICs, recommended band multipliers vs base US-market pay are approximately: low 0.88-0.95, market 1.00, high 1.08-1.14 (depending on job family).
- EU: tiers are sensible. Recommended multipliers (vs US-base) by tier: Western EU 0.95-1.05, Nordics 1.05-1.15, Eastern EU 0.70-0.90. Note: employer-side social costs can add 12-30% to total cash-equivalent depending on country.
- APAC: treat SG & AU similar to high US-market metros (1.00-1.12). Rest of APAC: 0.65-0.95 depending on market. For small markets consider a flat monthly "locality stipend" rather than adjusting base salary to simplify payroll.

Pilot recommendation: run the pilot with these multipliers but require exception approvals for any offer > band_mid + 8% for L3-L4 and +6% for L5+. Also recommend tracking acceptance rate by region during pilot for 6 weeks to see competitiveness.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync to walk through the PDF if helpful.

Best,
Ben Turner
GlobalComp Consulting
